messages:
Sasha: Hey — noticed an uptick in small factual hallucinations and occasional latency spikes on the AWQ canary we pushed last night. Group=32 + act-quant enabled. Example: model confidently responded 'Berlin is capital of Spain' in a short QA run. Anyone else seeing similar regressions?
Maya: Can you paste the eval diff and a few example prompts? also which model variant + quant config? :thinking_face:
Sasha: Model: rwd-13b-v1, canary tag awq-2026-03-01. Quick sample prompt list: 'What is the capital of Germany?', 'Who wrote Hamlet?'. Failures mostly short fact Q/A and some instruct-style completions are more verbose and off. Latency spike correlated with some nodes hitting higher p99.
Kevin: Ran a 1k eval split (squad-like + summarization). Quick numbers vs fp16 baseline: QA EM -4.2%, Rouge-L -0.6%, Perplexity ~+0.8. So accuracy hit on short exact-match tasks. Throughput looked ok except a couple of step spikes.
Maya: hmm that EM drop is non-trivial. Did you try toggling group_size / act quant?
Kevin: I did a small sweep. Results: group=16 + actq=true -> EM -1.1%. group=64 + actq=true -> EM -5.0%. group=32 + actq=false -> EM -0.9%. Looks like act quant is amplifying error for group sizes around 32-64 on this model.
Sasha: here's the exact AWQ config we rolled: ```
quant_backend: awq
group_size: 32
act_quant: true
act_block: 128
act_dtype: int8
```
Maya: Thanks. Two hypotheses: (1) act-ordering/scale interaction with group boundaries causing quant noise in early layers, (2) a sampling seed effect that surfaces on short QA tasks. We should reproduce with deterministic runs.
Ops-bot: [deploy-bot] Canary rollout awq-2026-03-01 -> 12/50 nodes stable, 3 failed (OOM on gpu-07), 2 degraded (p99 latency > 450ms).
Julie: +1 to deterministic runs. Can someone run the eval harness with identical seed and longer beam/temperature checks? Command: `./eval/run.sh --model rwd-13b-v1 --quant awq --group 32 --actq true --seed 1234 --evals qa,summ --out qa_awq_group32_seed1234.json`
Arjun: For production customers hitting correctness regressions we should auto-fallback to GPTQ-8 or fp16 for the QA/low-latency route until we sort AWQ. Suggest rollout policy: canary -> if QA EM delta <= 2% and p99 latency < 350ms continue, else rollback.
Maya: Agreed. Also try act_quant=false and group_size=16 as a middle ground. Kevin, can you capture the activation distributions (pre-quant) for first 3 layers — histogram + min/max? That'll tell us if clipping/truncation is the culprit.
Kevin: Will run activation dump with `TORCH_DUMP_ACTIVATIONS=1 python -m serve.bench --model rwd-13b-v1 --quant awq --group 32 --sample 200`. I'll post histograms in a follow-up. ETA 30m.
Sasha: Meanwhile I paused the rest of the canary traffic and pinrolled the safe variant (group=16, actq=false) for the affected routes. Notifying SRE. :white_check_mark:
Ops-bot: [alert] Canary traffic paused for awq-2026-03-01 at 2026-03-02T04:12:08Z by Sasha.
Julie: Once Kevin posts histograms, I'll run the eval harness with the act range clipping tweak Maya suggested: `act_clip: 6.0` and try act_order changes.
Arjun: Long-term: we may need to add an AWQ "robustness" profile that disables act-quant for early layers and lowers group size by default for QA-heavy workloads. Could be part of Optimize recommendations.
Maya: Agreed — also add an eval gate: any new quant profile must pass a short QA smoke set (50 queries) with EM delta < 2% before >5% traffic. I'll draft the gating PR.
Kevin: Uploaded initial histograms + per-layer min/max to the thread (link). Early layers have heavier tails than expected, clipping threshold probably too low with current act quant params.
Sasha: thanks — re-run with proposed clip and group=16, post results; if EM goes back within 2% we'll re-run a controlled canary.
Julie: ack, I'll coordinate the canary once we have confirmed numbers.
Arjun: If we end up reverting, let's note this as a regression in the quant bakeoff doc and tag the AWQ PR for follow-up. :memo:
Maya: I'll open the gating PR and add the QA smoke tests. Good catch everyone. :tada:
